- **Fahrtenbuch analysis, slice B — the trip analysis engine (`src/utils/tripAnalysis/`, PR #103), what to know:**
  - The plan is `fahrtenbuch-analysis.md` (22.09.2026, Arabic) over the owner's spec `fahrtenbuch.md` v2. Slice A (import reliability, migration `20260922100000`) and slices C/D (settings table `20260922110000` and the Fahrtenanalyse screen) are built in parallel; D builds against `types.ts`, which is the contract. Nothing imports the folder yet, so it is not in the bundle, and the "every file under `src/` is reachable" claim holds again only once D lands.
  - Pure TypeScript: no database, no UI, no clock (`Date.now()` is never called), so the same input gives the same result. `analyzeTrips(input)` takes a period's trips, the recorded shifts and per-driver budget inputs, and returns blocks, time metrics, findings (`Issue`: type, severity, evidence ids, values, German explanation, confidence, status `passed` / `conflict` / `unverifiable`) and per-check tallies.
  - **It only reads and reports.** Every output trip is the input object itself; no field proposes a new driver, a time or a price; `boundary.test.ts` proves it per id on a deep-frozen input, and fails if the folder ever references `assignRegularDriversToVehicleBlocks`, `assignSurplusBlocksToInhaberWithoutTimeChange`, `shiftOverlappingInhaberBlocks`, `assignBlocksPhase3`, `repairFinalOverlaps` or `extendShiftsForSalary`.
  - The rules: blocks per driver, where a gap **greater** than `blockGapMinutes` splits and an equal one stays, measured from the running maximum end; a vehicle change splits (an unknown vehicle is a value of its own); a midnight trip stays whole. Overlaps are a sweep over half-open intervals, every pair, per driver across vehicles and per vehicle across drivers. Travel between consecutive trips asks an injected estimator: `required = estimate + travelMarginMinutes`; the default has no routing service, so every travel check is `unverifiable`, never `passed`, and a gap below the margin alone is only a weak signal. The budget is exact (BigInt decimals, never a float division) and floored to whole minutes: 1000 / 13.9 → 4316 min, reserve 5 → 4016; `205 / 12.5` is the case where a float floor loses a minute. An unset reserve is "not set", never 0. Past activity is compared with `hoursMax`; the reserve is not deducted from it.
  - Statuses: `completed` is analysed; `cancelled` is kept and counted but never in time metrics (the sample's 44 cancelled rows carry no start or end); `unknown` is kept and on the review list. Rows missing a driver, a start or an end, with an end before the start, or with a DST-ambiguous local time are kept, with their reasons, and listed for review.
  - `analysisTripFromRow` adapts today's `fahrtenbuch_trips` rows through `resolveActualRideWindow` and departs from it in three tested places: a row with only one full date-time keeps that side instead of falling back to `trip_date` (column D, the day-early bug); the `trip_date + HH:MM` fallback adds a calendar day, not 24 h — **the resolver's fixed 24 h is 80 minutes on the March DST Sunday, and that resolver still feeds `FinalizePlanningModal`'s checks for rows without source date-times**; equal HH:MM is a trip under a minute, not 24 hours. It reads slice A's `start_at` / `end_at` / `currency` when a row carries them. **Guessed:** slice A's explicit status column is read as `trip_status`; rename it in the adapter if A names it otherwise. For older rows only `abgeschlossen` and `completed` mean completed; anything else, an empty status included, is `unknown`.
  - Not built here: clipping to the month (a trip across the month boundary counts whole); name-keyed identities for drivers without `original_driver_id` (their rows go to review); reading shifts out of `saved_stundennachweise.rows_json` (the screen converts them to `AnalysisShift`).
  - Tests: 77 in 7 files. The 10,000-trip benchmark prints its measurement on every run; see the PR for the figures and the machine load they were taken under.
- **Company roles (slice B, PR #117, migration `20260923120000`, in review), what to know:**
  - **What it opens.** `roles_name_key` was `UNIQUE (name)` across every company, so two companies could not both call a role `Disponent`. That is why no company has ever created one: production holds four roles, all system rows, and all 29 accounts sit on one of them. It is replaced by two partial unique indexes — one per name over the system rows, one per company, case- and whitespace-insensitive.
  - **Why relaxing it alone would have been a privilege escalation.** `sync_user_profile_role` copies `roles.name` into `user_profiles.role`, and that text is read as an authority by `is_company_admin()`, by `AuthContext.isAdmin` and by the activation-code mail's recipient list. A company role named `admin` would therefore have made its holders administrators **by name**, with no permission row anywhere. `app_private.enforce_company_role_shape` refuses that, plus `is_system` on a company role and any later change of kind; `app_private.enforce_user_profile_role_scope` closes the other half, because the privilege guard says *who* may change `role_id` and never *what* it may be set to.
  - **Two defects the proof found, both fixed here.** (1) `enforce_company_role_shape` and `company_role_save` both run as the **caller**, and both read helpers that were in `app_private`, where `authenticated` holds neither USAGE nor EXECUTE. Measured in a throwaway PostgreSQL 16: a company admin's plain `INSERT INTO roles` died with `42501 permission denied for function role_name_is_system_reserved`, and the RPC caught that same 42501 as `insufficient_privilege` and answered `not_authorized` — the feature could not work for anybody and the message blamed the administrator's own role. Both helpers are in `public` now, granted to `authenticated` and `service_role`. (2) `can_edit` without `can_view` was not refused when `can_view` was simply **absent**: `v_entry -> 'can_view'` is SQL NULL, so the guard's condition was NULL and `IF NULL THEN` never fired. All four comparisons are `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` now.
  - **The screen half was WIP and had a third.** `RoleModal` handed `RolesManagement` a *list* where `permissionPayload()` expects a *map*, so every one of the sixteen lookups came back `undefined` and the role saved with **no permissions at all** — every holder locked out of every page, with a success toast. That was the one TypeScript error above the 213 baseline. `templates` was passed and not declared (the "Als Kopie von" picker is wired now), and a system role offered a Save the RPC answers `not_found` for (it opens read-only now).
  - **What the proof is.** `tests/rls/company-roles.sql`, 167 assertions, dry-run against a stand-in of the live schema with **eight negative controls, every one caught**. Section 2f builds the escalation with the trigger off and shows `is_company_admin()` answering true for an account with no permission row, rather than only asserting the refusal; section 4d separates the two mechanisms behind the one `not_authorized` (a `WITH CHECK` 42501 against a silent `rows 0`), each with the administrator's version beside it. `src/utils/rolePageKeys.test.ts` pins `role_page_keys()` against `PAGE_DEFINITIONS` the way `planFeatures.test.ts` pins the feature map, and it matters for the reason slice C wrote down: `company_role_save` replaces a role's permission rows wholesale, so a stored key this build does not know is dropped the first time anyone edits that role.
  - **matrix.sql will never speak for these two RPCs.** Its uncovered sweep filters on `p.prosecdef` and both are SECURITY INVOKER — correctly, since RLS is meant to stay the boundary. Both are written into the rpc section by hand, with a fixture role of their own, and the header now says that a silent run is not evidence that the next SECURITY INVOKER function is covered.
  - **Not run here:** the RLS kit needs Docker and this machine has none. `tests/rls/company-roles.sql` is new and `matrix.sql` moved; run `npm run test:rls` on the VPS before merging.

- **Permission coverage (slice C, PR #110, migration `20260923130000`, in review), what to know:**
  - **What it closes.** 3.3 gave every tenant table one shape and carried exactly the role gates `20260910120000` had written — ten tables and the `salary-receipts` bucket — and said so in its own table list: *"no role gate today, and none added: a viewer writes these exactly as it does now."* So a `viewer`, the role with `can_edit` on none of the sixteen pages, imported a Fahrtenbuch, applied and finalized a month's planning, edited a historical reconciliation, saved a Stundennachweis and reassigned a trip. `matrix.sql` recorded it under "Recorded without a plan step".
  - **The mapping is to existing page keys only, and that is a decision about the Rollen screen, not about taste.** `RolesManagement.handleSaveRole` saves a role by **deleting every `role_permissions` row it has** and re-inserting one per key in `PAGE_DEFINITIONS`. A key the screen does not know is therefore dropped the first time anyone edits that role — silently, per role. So a new page key seeded by a migration is a landmine, and the slice introduces none. If a future slice does want one (a *Monatsplanung* page is the obvious candidate), it has to ship the `PAGE_DEFINITIONS` entry and the two dictionary keys **in the same release**, and even then the delete-and-reinsert makes the ordering delicate.
  - **Who loses what.** `admin` and `supervisor`: nothing — both hold `can_edit` on all sixteen pages. `editor`: the `documents` group (Fahrtenbuch, planning, historical, Stundennachweis, templates, blocks, variables) and the five planning RPCs, because `editor` has held `can_edit = false` on Dokumente since 20260302065621. `viewer`: all of it, which is the hole. **The query in the PR is how that is measured on a copy of production** — it returns one row per active account affected, and an empty result is the proof.
  - **The RPCs are the other half.** `apply_monthly_planning_run`, `replace_monthly_planning_run`, `delete_or_archive_monthly_planning_run`, `purge_old_monthly_planning_runs` and `reassign_fahrtenbuch_trip` are SECURITY DEFINER and run past RLS, so gating the tables alone closes the door and leaves the window open. Each asks `current_role_permits('documents', true)` **after** its own `caller has no company` branch, so the state refusal still comes first. The three Gehaltsquittung RPCs already asked their page. The four Abrechnung readers need no gate and are not touched: they are SECURITY INVOKER, asserted in the kit rather than assumed.
  - **Two things a later migration must not undo.** Deleting an import or a trip stays `is_company_admin()` alone — replacing that with the page would *widen* it, because a supervisor holds `can_edit` everywhere. And the `imported_by = auth.uid()` / `changed_by = auth.uid()` INSERT clauses sit **beside** the page gate, not instead of it: a page says whether you may write, never as whom.
  - **Not run here:** the RLS kit needs Docker, and the development machine has none. `tests/rls/permission-coverage.sql` is new, and `matrix.sql`, `tenant-state.sql` and `platform-contexts.sql` moved with it; run `npm run test:rls` on the VPS before merging.
- **Fahrtenbuch import reliability (Fahrtenanalyse slice A, PR #104, in review), what to know:**
  - **Additive only.** Migration `20260922100000` adds to `fahrtenbuch_trips` `start_at`/`end_at`/`time_zone`/`time_source`, `trip_status`, `needs_review`/`review_reasons`, `currency`/`currency_source` and a derived `source_row_key` with `source_row_key_basis`; to `fahrtenbuch_imports` `file_sha256`. `trip_date`, `start_time`, `end_time`, `duration_minutes` and every amount keep their meaning. `protect_fahrtenbuch_immutable_fields` is restated with 20260606035519's 21 comparisons carried verbatim and the 11 new columns appended; the migration fires it on a scratch copy of the table (self-check 1b). No `SCHEMA_EPOCH` bump: every new column is nullable or defaulted, and the previous release's inserts still pass the checks.
  - **The parser is `src/utils/fahrtenbuchImportParser.ts`** (moved out of the modal, 41 tests). Its SQL twin is the `app_private.fahrtenbuch_*` helpers; the parser test reads the migration and fails when the token lists, reject fragments, timestamp patterns, review reasons, time sources or statuses part. On the August 2026 sample the two derived identical `start_at`/`end_at`/`time_source` for all 2209 rows.
  - **Dedup:** the file's SHA-256 is unique per company (`fahrtenbuch_imports_company_file_sha256_key`) and immutable (`fahrtenbuch_imports_keep_file_sha256`); the ride key is unique per company where set (`fahrtenbuch_trips_company_source_row_key`). The key is B + driver + plate when the order-transmission column exists, else start + driver + plate — B alone would refuse the second of two rides sharing a second. Rows stored before the migration have no key, so the index cannot refuse a re-import of an *old* file's rides; the file hash cannot either (old imports have none). Replacing an import with the identical file means deleting it first.
  - **Behaviour the legacy screens now see:** incomplete rows are stored (flagged) instead of dropped, so a month with a ride lacking a start or end now fails `FinalizePlanningModal`'s pre-flight until someone deals with it; an `unknown`-status ride has `is_canceled = false`, so planning treats it as a ride. `reassign_fahrtenbuch_trip` cannot reassign a ride without times (its audit row needs them) — that was already true of cancelled rows.
  - **Measuring the backfill on a production-sized copy** (production itself is never touched): restore the newest nightly `/var/backups/ya-mobility/ya-YYYY-MM-DD.sql.gz` into a throwaway `supabase/postgres:17.6.1.170` container with `--network none`, under the RLS kit's flock, as the 17.09 rehearsal did; then `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --single-transaction` the pending migrations in order, with this file last, wrapped so it ends in `ROLLBACK`, and read the `NOTICE: fahrtenbuch import facts backfilled: {...}` line — rows, per `time_source`, per `trip_status`, needs review — and `\timing` for the lock length. Delete the container. A cheaper read-only estimate on production itself (no function needed): `SELECT count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE raw_data_json ->> 'Uhrzeit des Fahrtbeginns' ~ '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2} [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}') FROM fahrtenbuch_trips;` — the second number is roughly the rows that will get `source_start_end`.
  - **Lock:** ADD COLUMN takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on `fahrtenbuch_trips` for the whole transaction, backfill included. 100 000 synthetic trips took 1 min 55 s in a one-CPU container under Docker Desktop; the first two designs took 16 and 6 minutes (per-trip column resolution, and a single statement whose join the planner rescanned) — keep the keyed scratch table if you touch it.
  - **The RLS kit ran on the dev machine** for the first time (Docker Desktop, `node scripts/rls-test.mjs`): all files pass, `matrix.sql` unchanged, no `UNCOVERED` line.
- **Two edit defects found by phase 5, fixed (this PR), what to know:**
  - **An Inhaber edited on the Fahrer screen was saved as an employee.** `useDatabase.getDrivers()` mapped every column the edit form reads except `employment_type`, so `DriverModal` opened each driver with `driver.employment_type ?? 'employee'` and `planningToDb` wrote `'employee'` back on the next save of any field; planning then applied the hour limits an Inhaber is exempt from. The list read now goes through `mapDriverRow()` (`src/lib/driverRow.ts`, pinned by `driverRow.test.ts`), which carries it; the create and update paths already did. Production on 22.09.2026: 4 `company_owner` drivers in 2 companies. **Rows flipped before the fix cannot be found** — `drivers` has no `updated_at` — so the owner should check which of his drivers are Inhaber. Batch 1b's `flows-batch1b.mjs` pinned the old behaviour on purpose; move that pin when both are on staging.

Now `password?.trim()`, with the parameter typed optional as `UserModal`'s `onSave` already declares it. Batch 4's `flows-batch4.mjs` pinned the old behaviour; move that pin too.

  - Double booking: the request id is written to the tab sessionStorage the moment the request leaves, reused on retry and after a reload, and cleared on a definitive answer. Closing while the outcome is unknown goes through a confirmation. What it cannot cover: another tab, another browser, or cleared storage. A database-side guard is an open owner question.

- **Overlapping salary rows (PR #71), what to know:**
  - The owner decided on 17.09.2026 that he merges overlapping salary rows by hand before paying, and that `confirm_salary_cash_payment`'s `overlapping_salary` refusal stays. PR #71 makes them findable: an amber badge beside the driver's name on the Gehälter screen, naming each overlapping row's period and amount. No query is added — it is folded out of the rows the screen already loads, in one `useMemo`. `src/utils/salaryPeriodOverlap.ts` is the pure detection, 19 tests.
  - **How they are created, established before proposing to prevent them.** Exactly two paths write a `salaries` row, both a click on the Gehälter screen: `SalariesManagement.tsx:301` (mark paid/unpaid) and `SalaryDetailsModal.tsx:119` (`ensureSalaryExists`, which fires *automatically* when the payments dialog opens on a driver with no row for that period). Nothing else — no import, no planning run, no Abrechnung, no edge function, no trigger, no RPC. Every period the app itself computes is a **business month** (`getBusinessMonthRange`, whose calendar-month fallback is unreachable), and consecutive business months never overlap. The overlap comes from the two free-form date inputs at `SalariesManagement.tsx:449-475`, which write any pair of dates unvalidated, past a `unique_driver_period` that covers only `period_start`. **So overlaps are hand-entry, not a supported flow** — a guard in the write path would break nothing that exists today.
  - ~~**There is no way to merge the rows in the product.**~~ — closed by PR #73, below: the Gehälter screen now **deletes** a salary row, which is the whole merge. Until then, "by hand" meant a direct database edit. #71's own follow-up question, "whether the screen should grow a delete for a salary with no payments", is answered yes and built; editing a period was built, reviewed and **removed**, for the reasons in that entry.
  - **Preventing new ones is proposed, not built**, and written up in PR #71's body for the owner: an application check at the two insert sites first, then a BEFORE INSERT (not UPDATE — merging needs edits) trigger, and **against** an exclusion constraint, which validates the whole table on `ADD CONSTRAINT` and so could not ship while any company still holds an overlap, raises on an inverted period, and would need a `SCHEMA_EPOCH` bump.
- **Button label contrast (PR #72), what to know:**
  - **The trap, because it will be walked into again.** `--accent` is the accent *background*; `--accent-text` is accent-coloured *text for a normal background*. The names read as a pair and are not one. In the light theme both hold `#2563eb`, so `background: var(--accent)` with `color: var(--accent-text)` painted the label in the button's own colour — **1.00:1, the text simply absent**; in the dark theme `#22d3ee` on `#06b6d4`, 1.34:1. The owner hit both on staging. The token for a label on a filled background is `--text-inverse`, which `.btn-primary` in `index.css` has always used and which was **the only pairing in the codebase that already passed**.
  - 73 label colours in 40 files now use it: `--accent-text` on `--accent` (9 sites, 1.00/1.34 → 5.17/7.31), white on `--accent` (58, 5.17/2.43 → 5.17/7.31), white on `--danger` (6, 4.83/3.76 → 4.83/4.71). **The light theme does not move** — `--text-inverse` is `#ffffff` there, which 58 of these sites already spelled literally; only the dark theme changes, and only from failing to passing. `--accent-text` keeps its 91 correct uses on neutral surfaces, four of which are now pinned as well.
  - ~~**`--success` and `--warning` are the open half — 18 sites, and no token fixes them.**~~ — closed by PR #76, below. White reached only 3.77:1 on `--success` and 3.19:1 on `--warning` in the light theme, and `--text-inverse` *is* white there, so it changed nothing: the background was too light for any legible label. Both were also failing as text on their own `-subtle` fills (3.58:1 and 3.07:1). The owner approved darkening them on 17.09.2026.
  - **Two guards, and both were proved to fail before being trusted.** `tokens.contrast.test.ts` now parses the legacy hex blocks as well as the Phase-2 RGB ones — hence the two new `/* @legacy-tokens light|dark */` markers in `index.css` — and holds `--text-inverse` on accent/accent-hover/danger to 4.5:1 (breaking `--text-inverse` fails 3 tests). `accentLabel.contrast.test.ts` reads the source and refuses the pairing at the call site, in files the token test never opens (restoring one site names `components/SalaryDetailsModal.tsx:699`). Both carry the reasoning in a header comment so the next reader does not "fix" them; the second also self-checks that it can still see style objects, so a broken parser cannot pass by finding nothing.
  - **How the sites were found, because grep is not enough here.** A scanner parses `index.css` into both theme tables, walks every balanced `{…}` style object skipping strings and comments, splits conditional values per branch, resolves each `var(--x)` per theme, composites translucent values and computes the WCAG ratio. A two-line grep window reported ~7 defects; a 14-line window found 12 candidates of which **3 were false positives** (the importer's step bar carries no text, its label sits on the modal background; the OTP resend link's `--accent-text` branch has no background). Every hit was read in source before being changed. Disabled branches were left alone on purpose — `--text-tertiary` on `--bg-muted` is 2.24:1, but WCAG 1.4.3 exempts inactive controls and "fixing" it makes disabled buttons look enabled.
  - **What it did not do:** no screen was rendered. Every figure is computed from the token values; nothing was checked in a browser or on the VPS. The scan also turned up ~200 **hardcoded hex** colours (e.g. `#b91c1c` on `rgba(220,38,38,0.06)`) that read acceptably in light and badly in dark because they are theme-blind literals — a separate, larger defect class, reported and untouched. **Still true after PR #76, and the owner deferred them to phase 5 on 17.09.2026. Do not pick them up piecemeal.**
- **Darkened `--success` and `--warning` (PR #76), what to know:**
  - **The owner's decision of 17.09.2026**, and the other half of #72. The light values moved `#059669 → #0A7A45` and `#d97706 → #8F5200`; the dark values did **not** move.
  - **One token could not carry both roles, and the reason is arithmetic, not taste.** In the dark theme a white label needs the fill at relative luminance ≤ 0.183, while reading as text on `--bg-surface` (`#111827`) needs the token at ≥ 0.237. The windows do not overlap, at any hue. So the fill got its own token — **`--success-solid` and `--warning-solid`**, named after `--critical-solid`, which is the Phase-2 block's answer to exactly this problem. In the **light** theme both roles want the same darkness, so there the two tokens hold one value; the split exists only where it is forced. `--success` / `--warning` stay the text colour, and that is still their job at ~200 call sites.
  - **The measured ratios**, all now pinned. Light: white on the fill 3.77 → **5.41** (success) and 3.19 → **6.22** (warning); text on `--bg-surface` 3.77 → **5.41** / 3.19 → **6.22**; text on the `-subtle` fill 3.58 → **5.13** / 3.07 → **6.00**; worst light role 5.00 / 5.75. Dark: white on the fill 2.54 → **4.88** and 2.15 → **4.88** (through the new `-solid` tokens `#0B824A` / `#A85F00`, whose lightness is the balance point where the 4.5:1 label margin and the 3:1 shape margin are equal); the text roles were already 5.35–8.93 and are unchanged.
  - **26 call sites, not 18.** #72's list counted only style objects with an explicit `color` entry; nine more spell the label as Tailwind's `text-white` in the className, and a 26th is a **hover handler** (`SalaryDetailsModal.tsx:906`) that assigns the fill imperatively, where no style object holds it. `PlatformLoginPage.tsx:179` from that list is gone — PR #74 deleted the file. Each site changed one token name in the background position only; no className, no layout, no component.
  - **Hue: say plainly what this does and does not fix.** Green still reads as green and amber as amber to normal vision. For **red/green colour blindness it fixes nothing, and nothing could.** Simulating the trio (Viénot 1999) shows today's `--success`/`--danger` already collapse to 1.01:1 under deuteranopia — indistinguishable *before* this change. A 2803 × 2133 search over every green and amber that passes all the contrast roles puts the ceiling at 1.46:1, and that optimum demands a `#532209` that no longer reads as amber at all. The cause is the constraint itself: once all three status colours must be dark enough for a white label they share one narrow lightness band, and lightness is the only channel a dichromat has left. **So the mitigation is that nothing relies on hue**, which was verified site by site: every filled button carries a German label and a lucide icon (`Download` + "Excel", `Plus` + "Neuer Check", `Save`, `CheckCircle`), and every count badge carries its number. The one fill with no text is the discount-code toggle, where the white knob now reaches 5.41:1 against the track instead of 2.54:1.
  - **Why these two values.** They are the Phase-2 `--positive` and `--caution`, which the owner already approved for the prototype and which `tokens.contrast.test.ts` already guards. The legacy and Phase-2 palettes now agree on what success and warning are, so Phase 5 moves a screen across without re-deciding the colour. They were not picked for colour-blind separation, because as shown above no available value buys any.
  - **The guard, proved to fail three ways before being trusted.** `tokens.contrast.test.ts` gained **40** legacy checks (112 → 152 cases) and `accentLabel.contrast.test.ts` two more: `--success`/`--warning` as text on the four `--bg-*` surfaces, the same on their own `-subtle` fills, a **white** label (not `--text-inverse` — no call site uses it) on each `-solid`, and each `-solid` at 3:1 against `--bg-surface` and `--bg-elevated` for SC 1.4.11. It also learned to parse `rgba(…)` and composite it, because the dark `-subtle` fills are translucent and were never measured before. `accentLabel.contrast.test.ts` gained the call-site half: a filled background naming `--success`/`--warning` instead of the `-solid` twin is an offence, in the style-object form and the imperative hover form. Proofs: restoring the old light `--success` fails **8** tests; lightening dark `--success-solid` back to the text value fails the white-label test; pointing two fills back at the text token names `components/SalaryDetailsModal.tsx:906` and `pages/WerkstattPage.tsx:193`. Both new blocks carry their reasoning in a header comment, and the call-site rule self-checks that it can still see a `-solid` fill, so a broken parser cannot pass by finding nothing.
  - **What it did not do:** **no screen was rendered.** Every figure is computed from the token values; nothing was opened in a browser or on the VPS, and the dark theme in particular changes the look of ten filled buttons that nobody has seen. Check `Werkstatt`, `Bargeldbestand`, `Belege` and the admin dashboard's amber count badges on staging after the deploy.
  - ~~**One finding left open, deliberately.** `--danger` on `--danger-subtle` is **4.41:1 light and 3.87:1 dark**.~~ — closed by PR #79, below, on the owner's decision of 18.09.2026.
- **Darkened `--danger` (PR #79), what to know:**
  - **The owner's decision of 18.09.2026**, and the last of the three status colours. Light `#dc2626 → #C0262D`; dark `#ef4444 → #FF8A8A` for the text role, with a new `--danger-solid` at `#D63A40` for the fill. These are the Phase-2 `--critical` and `--critical-solid` unchanged, already approved for the prototype and already guarded, so the legacy and Phase-2 palettes now agree on all three statuses and phase 5 moves a screen across without re-deciding a colour.
  - **The defect was wider than the one finding named it.** #76 measured `--danger` on its own `-subtle` fill at 4.41 light / 3.87 dark. Measuring every surface the token actually renders on found **three more failing dark pairs** that nothing had ever checked: on `--bg-elevated` **4.21**, and on `--danger-subtle` over `--bg-surface` **4.34** and over `--bg-subtle` **4.11**. Eight failing roles, not two.
  - **Where the split was needed, checked rather than assumed.** The dark theme only, as for the other two, and with a wider gap: a white label needs the fill at relative luminance ≤ **0.1833**, while the text role needs ≥ **0.2741** — the binding surface is `--danger-subtle` composited over `--bg-elevated`, not `--bg-surface` as for success and warning. In the **light** theme one value serves both: the fill needs ≤ 0.1833 and the text role ≤ 0.1633, so the text constraint is strictly tighter and `--danger` and `--danger-solid` hold the same `#C0262D`.
  - **The measured ratios.** Light — text on the four `--bg-*` surfaces 4.46/4.83/4.83/4.59 → **5.46/5.90/5.90/5.61**; text on `--danger-subtle` 4.41 → **5.40**; a white label on the fill 4.83 → **5.90**; shape against the surface 4.83 → **5.90**. Dark — text on the surfaces 5.10/4.71/4.21/4.48 → **8.45/7.82/6.99/7.43**; text on `--danger-subtle` over them 4.71/4.34/3.87/4.11 → **7.81/7.20/6.42/6.81**; a white label on `--danger-solid` **4.63**; `--danger-solid` as a shape 3.83 and 3.43, both over the 3:1 of SC 1.4.11. `--danger-subtle` itself does **not** move, in either theme: the dark wash is the same hue (0°) as the new text colour and reaches 6.42–7.81 under it, so repainting some forty badges would buy nothing.
  - **One role gets very slightly worse, and it is the honest trade.** The six destructive buttons that PR #72 had put on `--text-inverse` read 4.71 in the dark theme; as a white label on `--danger-solid` they read **4.63**. Both clear 4.5. What the swap buys is that the *text* role stops failing at all, and that all three statuses now spell a filled button the same way. `--text-inverse` is #111827 in the dark theme and would be **3.83:1** on `--danger-solid`, so the earlier shape is now a defect and the call-site guard refuses it by name.
  - **Nine call sites, and three of them were invisible to #76's scanner.** Six spell the fill directly (`FahrtenbuchImportModal.tsx:1232`, `FahrtenbuchTripsView.tsx:531`, `TrialBanner.tsx:92`, `CompaniesPage.tsx:966` and `:983`, `SuperAdminDashboard.tsx:1581`); three reach it through a **name** — `CompaniesPage.tsx:268` via `btnColor`, `TrialBanner.tsx:59` via a new `fill` const, `ConfirmationModal.tsx:117` via `getConfirmBgColor()`. Those same three sites also carried **three `--warning` fills and one `--success` fill that PR #76 missed** — it read literals only, so its guard reported `[]` while they stood. The scanner now resolves a background written as a bare identifier or a zero-argument call back to its `const` initializer.
  - **Hue.** `#C0262D` is hue 357°, saturation 67%, lightness 45% — a crimson, not a brown or a maroon; `#dc2626` was hue 0°, 72%, 51%. Dark `#D63A40` is hue 358°, 66%, 53%. A destructive button still reads as red. For red/green colour blindness the picture is unchanged and still bad: simulated (Viénot 1999), `--warning` against `--danger` is **1.05:1** under deuteranopia in the dark theme and **1.20:1** under protanopia in the light one. **So hue carries nothing, and this was verified for the nine sites rather than asserted**: all nine carry a German text label; six also carry a lucide icon at all times (`RefreshCw`, `Trash2` ×3, `Zap` ×2), a seventh shows `RefreshCw` while the action runs (`CompaniesPage.tsx:268`), and the two with none — `SuperAdminDashboard.tsx:1581` *Ablehnen* and `ConfirmationModal.tsx:117`, whose label is the caller's — are still words, not colour. **No `--danger` control in the codebase is colour-only**: a sweep for small coloured shapes and for bar widths found none.
  - **The guard, 152 → 170 token cases plus 5 → 7 call-site cases, and proved to fail six ways.** Restoring the old light `--danger` fails **5** (`bg-base` and the four `-subtle` composites, at 4.46 and 4.41); restoring the old dark value fails **5** (`bg-elevated` 4.21, `bg-subtle` 4.48, and three `-subtle` composites); lightening `--danger-solid` to the text value fails the white-label test at **2.27**; pointing a direct site back at `var(--danger)` names `pages/CompaniesPage.tsx:966`; pointing the **indirect** `btnColor` back names `pages/CompaniesPage.tsx:268` — the proof the resolver is doing work; labelling a `-solid` fill with `--text-inverse` names `components/FahrtenbuchTripsView.tsx:531`. The resolver has its own two self-checks: a fixture that pins the ternary and the arrow-body shapes, and a count that it is still wired into the scan of real source.
  - **What left the token test on purpose.** `{ fg: 'text-inverse', bg: 'danger' }` — PR #72's answer to a white label failing on the dark `--danger`, which moved the *label* instead of the *fill*. Nothing pairs those two any more, and an assertion about a combination no screen renders reads as coverage without being any.
  - **What it did not do:** **no screen was rendered.** Every figure is computed from the token values. The light theme moves for the first time in this series — `--danger` is some 157 `color:` call sites, so every red word in the product is slightly darker — and the dark theme changes nine filled buttons and the colour of all that red text. Worth a look on staging at Fahrtenbuch (delete an import), Firmen (the lifecycle dialogs), the admin dashboard's *Ablehnen*, the trial banner, and any toast error.
- **Phase 5 batch 1b: Belege, Fahrer and Umsätze on the design system (PR #100, in review, branch `phase5/batch1b-belege-fahrer-umsaetze`, rebased onto staging after #96–#99 and #102), what to know:**
  - **The rest of batch 1, on batch 1's pattern.** `ReceiptList`, `ReceiptModal`, `BelegePage`, `DriversManagement`, `DriverModal`, `FahrerPage`, `IncomeManagement` and `UmsaetzePage` move onto `src/components/ui`, inside the unchanged `AppLayout`. The forms' selects are logic (`e.target.value`, `required`), so they use `NativeSelect` — batch 3's primitive since the rebase; batch 1b had built the same thing and took theirs, renaming its prop to `containerClassName`.
  - **Look only, proved per file as text.** `node design-harness/identity-proof.mjs . origin/staging <files>` compares each file's logic region (after the imports, before `// ── Presentation (phase 5)`) with the base line by line, and requires every inline `onX={…}` of the old markup and every call it made to something the logic declares, verbatim in the new file. Lines that left a logic region, all of them look: the `hoveredRow` state (ReceiptList, DriversManagement, IncomeManagement), the inline `inputStyle` objects (ReceiptList, ReceiptModal, DriverModal, IncomeManagement), ReceiptList's `SortIcon` and `formatDE` (euros go through `utils/money.ts`), and IncomeManagement's carousel refs and drag handlers, which wrote the carousel's cursor and scroll position and nothing else — the carousel is a per-driver table whose rows are `getWeeklyDataByDriver()`'s answer, as each card was. **Lines added:** one per page, `useDatabase()` also asked for `isConnected` (below), and in IncomeManagement exactly the three the load-failure rule allows. Everything else — every `supabase.from` chain, filter, order, parse, rounding, permission check and export — is the old text.
  - **The Belegnummer is still the system's.** `generateUniqueReceiptNumber()` (`BEL-{timestamp}-{random}`, checked against every loaded number) is untouched and `applyExtracted()` never writes it; `flows-batch1b.mjs` scans a Beleg and checks that the number the insert carries is the one the form generated before the scan. `RECEIPT_CATEGORIES`, `Tanken` included, and the payment-method values are the stored strings. The number field stays editable, as it was; making it read-only would be a behaviour change for its own PR.
  - **A figure whose load failed is not shown.** Belege and Fahrer read through `useDatabase`, which on a failed connection test serves the lists from local storage — which nothing writes — so the screens said "Keine Belege vorhanden" and 0,00 € for a database they never reached; the pages now read `isConnected` and show an error and no figure. Umsätze reads its drivers the same way, and its entries directly: **`IncomeManagement` has a `loadFailed` state** under the rule decided for batch 2 (cleared where `loadIncomes` starts, set in its existing catch), so a failed read of the entries alone withholds the total, the per-driver figures and the export. **Still swallowed:** a `getReceipts()`/`getDrivers()` read that fails after a good connection test falls back to local storage inside `useDatabase`; surfacing it is a change to the hook.
  - **Read contexts and roles.** Every write control asks the scope (`useCompanyScope()`, directly or through the page's `canEdit`/`canDelete`/`canCreate`): a platform `view` context and a viewer are offered no add, edit, delete or status toggle, and the flows check all three screens for both. Controls a caller may not use are hidden rather than disabled.
  - **Defects found by clicking.** (1) **Fixed by #102** while this was in review: `useDatabase.getDrivers()` did not map `employment_type`, so an Inhaber edited in the Fahrer form was saved as an employee; `mapDriverRow()` carries it now, the Fahrer list shows the *Inhaber* badge, and `flows-batch1b.mjs` pins the fixed behaviour (the edit keeps `company_owner`). (2) **Open:** the Belege week filter drops the week's Sunday — `getBusinessWeeksForMonth()` ends a week at Sunday 00:00 local time and `ReceiptList` compares `new Date(receipt.date)`, UTC midnight, 02:00 in Berlin — and with it that week's summary PDF; a fix to the filter logic, its own PR, pinned as it is in the flows. (3) **Open, small:** after a Beleg is added the form re-mounts (BelegePage's loading state unmounts it), so `resetForm(true)`'s "keep the driver" never shows.
  - **Rendered: 65 shots before and 65 after**, in `Docs/design/phase5/batch1b/{before,after}/`: the three screens at 375, 768 and 1280 in both themes; at 1280 light and 375 dark the add form, a scanned Beleg with two uncertain fields, both edit forms, the planning section, delete confirmations, the filter panel, the driver limit, empty, a failed connection, a failed read of the Umsätze entries alone, and read-only (a platform `view` context); one English shot per screen. The before set is `origin/staging`'s `src/` through this branch's harness (`--root`); the Fahrer before shots were retaken after the rebase, since #102 put the Inhaber badge on the legacy screen too. `flows-batch1b.mjs`: 27 checks, verified on each write's payload in `window.__harness.writes`. **Staging has not seen these screens.**
  - **Why captures stalled at the first 375 px shot.** Not the touch context. The harness's resolver swapped a real module for its fake by resolved path, and Vite resolves a URL the browser fetches with `<root>/index.html` as the importer — so the URL of a real module a fake re-exports was served the fake itself. The fake re-exported itself, `formatAmountDE` (imported by the Beleg form) was missing, the module graph failed to link, and since `main.tsx` imports every page the harness never booted. Every run's first shot is a 375 px one, hence the pattern. `vite.config.ts` now leaves URL requests alone. **The shared harness after the rebase:** batch 1b's rows live in `fixtures-batch1b.ts` and its shots in `shots-batch1b.mjs`, as batches 2 and 3 keep theirs; `fakes/supabase.ts` gained the write log (`window.__harness.writes`) and three one-line hooks; `capture.mjs` keeps staging's per-checkout cache, DOM-quiet settle and 600 s first page, and adds a warm-up, a hard cap per shot with one retry pass, and taller windows for `tall` dialog shots; `vite.config.ts` pre-bundles `lucide-react` and keeps its own cache per checkout for runs that do not go through `capture.mjs`. **Batches 2 and 3 were re-run on the merged harness** (`flows-batch2.mjs` 29 of 29, `flows-batch3.mjs` 20 of 20).
  - **Ratchets:** style 5871 → **5502** inline styles and 3402 → **3330** colours against staging after batches 2 and 3; the eight files count zero and the ratchet test pins them. Typecheck 221 → **219**: the Beleg modal's invented `style2` prop and `ConfirmationModal`'s `type="warning"` mismatch went with the old markup. **Contrast:** `caution` and `positive` on `field` at 3:1 (a field framed as uncertain or as ready to save; lowest 5.41:1) are new; `positive`, `critical` and `brand-text` as text on `sunken`, which the Beleg form's OCR diagnostics and drop zone render, are batch 2's pairs.

  - **Look only, and checked as text, not by eye.** Each component's body from its first line through `handleExport` (CarModal: through `handleRenewTuev`) is the old text verbatim; the new markup is appended below a `// ── Presentation (phase 5)` line and only draws. The check is a substring comparison of the old block against the new file, and it passes for all three. Two places mixed presentation into logic and were split rather than rewritten: `TUEV_CONFIG` in `CarsManagement.tsx` held the labels the Excel export reads **and** the colours and icons — the labels stayed, the look moved to `TUEV_PRESENTATION`; and `FixedCostsManagement.tsx` lost only its `hoveredRow` state and its `inputStyle` object. The vehicle form is a `Sheet`: Escape and the close button close it, a click beside it does not (the old overlay ignored both, and a stray click must not throw away a typed form). Fixkosten opens its add form from the page header and focuses the first field. That is what the export writes, so it stayed; it is audit finding 1's class and needs its own look. The Fixkosten debug line (audit finding 6) stays too, set as small print under the list, because Docs/design/README.md leaves removing it to the owner.
  - **Rendered, and how.** No staging: `design-harness/` renders the production `CarsPage` and `FixkostenPage` inside the production `AppLayout` on invented data, by swapping `src/lib/supabase.ts` and five context hooks at module resolution in its own Vite config, so nothing in `src/` knows about it. `npm run harness` serves it (`?screen=fahrzeuge|fixkosten&data=…&role=…&theme=…&lang=…`), `npm run harness:capture -- --set before|after [--root <checkout>]` takes the shots, and `npm run harness:flows` clicks every write and refusal through (15 checks: add with a driver, the required plate, the two-driver lock, edit, delete and cancel, the tabs, add/edit/delete a cost with the total following, the empty-field refusal, the viewer, the failed load, and every row action within a 375 px touch screen). Both shot sets come from the same harness and the same Chrome: the before set from a `git worktree` of the commit before the conversion, via `--root`. 34 each, in `Docs/design/phase5/batch1/{before,after}/`: both screens at 375, 768 and 1280 in both themes, ten states (form, delete, limit, empty, add, inline edit, viewer, missing table) at 1280 light and 375 dark, and one English shot per screen. The 375 shots emulate a touch phone, so the coarse-pointer sizes show.
  - **What rendering found that no test would have.** A CSS grid without `grid-cols-1` sizes its track to the widest child's min-content, so the tab row pushed the whole Fahrzeuge page past 375 px; `grid-cols-1` (`minmax(0,1fr)`) is now on every grid wrapper. At 375 px on a touch screen the icon buttons grow to 40 px and the table scrolled 13 px, hiding the delete button — the approved prototype has the same clipping — so the plate and status columns take tighter padding below `sm`. A text field in a table cell cannot shrink below its 20-character natural width, which pushed the inline edit's save/cancel off a phone; `size={1}` lets it take the cell's width. A Chrome with an English UI shows `mm/dd/yyyy` in a date field whatever the page's locale; the capture launches Chrome with `--lang=de-DE`.
  - **The style ratchet** (`scripts/style-ratchet.mjs`, rules and 16 tests in `style-ratchet-core.mjs` / `style-ratchet.test.ts`) counts, per file under `src/`, inline styles (`style={…}` and imperative `el.style.x =` writes, the legacy hover) and hard-coded colours (hex, `rgb()`/`hsl()` with a number, Tailwind palette classes, quoted `'white'`/`'black'`), after stripping comments. More than `style-baseline.json` fails, fewer fails and asks for `npm run styles:update`, per file so one screen cannot pay for another. It runs in `npm run build` after the typecheck ratchet. **6731 → 6607 inline styles and 3793 → 3774 colours** across 111 → 107 files; the five batch-1 files are at zero and a test pins them there. **Its cost is the typecheck ratchet's:** a PR merged while another is open can move a file the other's baseline records — PR #87 moved `PlatformTeamPage.tsx` from 50 to 67 while this branch was open — so rebase and run `npm run styles:update` before merging, and read the diff it writes. **And new code is still being written the legacy way:** PR #89 (3.10/3.11), merged while this was open, added 91 inline styles and 2 hard-coded colours in five new files (`AnnouncementBanner.tsx` and four under `components/settings/`). Once the ratchet is on staging, a new file like those fails the build; `npm run styles:update` would record it, so a review that sees a new or higher line in `style-baseline.json` should ask why the screen was not built on `src/components/ui` instead.
  - **Contrast pairs added to `tokens.contrast.test.ts`:** `fg` and `fg-muted` on `brand-soft`, `positive-soft`, `caution-soft` and `critical-soft` (Alert bodies, the selected driver row; lowest 6.60:1); `critical` on `sunken` at 3:1 (the delete icon's hover, 5.21:1); and a new block for the Phase-2 foregrounds on the **legacy** `--bg-base`, the page background a converted screen sits on until `AppLayout` moves — `fg`, `fg-muted`, `fg-subtle` and `critical` at 4.5:1 (lowest `fg-subtle` light, 4.96:1) and `brand` and `focus` at 3:1 (lowest `brand` dark, 4.18:1). 202 contrast cases, all passing.

- **Phase 5 batch 3: Dokumente, Monatsplanung and Stundennachweis on the design system, the display only (PR #99, in review, branch `phase5/batch3-dokumente-planung-stundennachweis`), what to know:**
  - **The frame moved, and nothing that computes, plans or builds a document.** Converted: `DocumentsPage` whole (header, the five tool cards, the archive, both delete dialogs, the Fahrtenbuch sub-view's header); `FahrtenbuchTripsView` whole (toolbar, filters, the import list, the summary as `KpiCard`s, the trips as a `DataTable` from `md` up and as cards on a phone, paging, the import delete); `MonatsplanungDriverPool` whole; `CompanyPlannerPage`'s frame (header, the mode choices, Phase 1's month/year/import fields, its four block parameters, the run button, `BlockStatusBanner`); `MonatsplanungAppliedRuns`' list, rows and delete dialog; and `StundennachweisPage`'s frame (header and its three actions, the progress bar, step 1, step 2, the waiting states). Whole components left legacy: `MonatsplanungAssignmentPreview` (Phases 3–5 and `handleApply`), `MonatsplanungStundennachweisPreview` (Lohnart, premiums, transfers), `FinalizePlanningModal` (the pre-flight checks and document generation), `HistoricalReconciliationWizard`, `HistoricalWorkingHoursWizard` (its dead `AutoShiftPlanView` untouched), `FahrtenbuchImportModal`.
  - **Proven as text, per file, by `design-harness/identity-batch3.mjs`** (`node design-harness/identity-batch3.mjs --base <base commit>`). For each file it compares the base commit's text with the working tree's: (1) every old line outside the declared redrawn ranges appears verbatim, in order, as the same contiguous chunks; (2) every expression the old markup evaluated — handlers, `disabled`/`value`/`min`/`max` guards, the condition in front of a conditional block, the collection a list is drawn from, formatting calls — appears in the new file, whitespace aside; (3) every old line that reads or writes data, calls the clock or `Math`, parses a number, formats a date or an amount, or checks a permission appears too. A loss must be listed as a drop with its reason, a listed drop that is not missing fails as a stale claim, and `mustContain` names where a dropped expression's figures went, so a drop cannot hide one. It also fails the branch if any file outside batch 3's allow-list changed. **Across the six files: 5645 of 7806 old lines verbatim, 668 expressions carried, 440 sensitive lines present, and every drop presentation** (colour maps, a style object, header-key loops, the card list split into `KpiCard`s, and `toLocaleString`/`toFixed` replaced by `formatEuro`). Negative controls: removing the company filter from the group delete, pointing "Öffnen" at the PDF handler, a clamp bound 120 → 121, the run button losing its import guard, the Fahrtenbuch download's year fallback and the admin test on an import's delete each fail it. As first written it had four faults of its own (it walked into style objects, read imports as markup, could not see an insertion, and compared `{…}` with `(…)`); they were fixed before it was trusted.
  - **What a figure says differently, all of it the way it is written:** euro amounts go through `utils/money.ts` — Dokumente's gross (a no-break space before €), the driver pool's salary range (`toFixed` wrote `2100.00 €`), the trips view's totals (`toLocaleString` with only a minimum of two digits printed a float sum with three, `20.990,855 €`) and a phone card's fare (a US decimal point). **Dates were left exactly as they were**, including the archive's `new Date(…).toLocaleDateString('de-DE')`, which writes `4.9.2026` rather than `04.09.2026` — a display rule, but a date call, and this batch does not move date calls; a follow-up.
  - **Behaviour that changed, all of it presentation.** The delete dialogs (a record, a month, a planning run, an import) are Radix dialogs: Escape and a click outside mean Abbrechen, and all four still refuse to close while their delete runs and still show a failure inside themselves — so none is `ConfirmDialog`, which closes on confirm. Dokumente's month header is a button of its own (`aria-expanded`); a click on the row's empty space no longer folds it. The Stundennachweis back button has a name ("Zurück", audit finding 3). Step 2's tabs are Radix tabs driven only by the original `onClick`s (`activationMode="manual"`, no `onValueChange`). A failed driver read in the pool shows its error without seven counts of zero. The trips view keeps a card per trip on a phone, because the table under `md` would have dropped status, plate and route.
  - **Found, not fixed, because each is logic:** Dokumente's archive read ignores its error, so a failed read shows "Keine gespeicherten Stundennachweise vorhanden"; the Stundennachweis driver read does the same (an empty driver list); `useFahrtenbuch.fetchImports` throws a failed read into callers that do not catch it. - **Bargeldbestand on the cash ledger (PR #43, plan 4.3b), what to know:**
  - `BargeldbestandPage` and the Overview cash panel read `cash_movements` through `utils/cashLedger.ts`. Both establish scope before making any claim: `cash_movements` and `salary_cash_receipts` are readable by the owning company only, so platform staff inside a customer read that customer's Bargeld and Belege and none of its movements. An empty set there is indistinguishable from "no payouts", so out of scope the payout card is dropped, the older "Bargeld − Belege" label kept, and the caveat carried into the Excel dump. Printing 0,00 € would have turned a missing read into a false claim.
  - Five defects from the review, all fixed before merge: a literal minus prefixed to an already-signed number (a receipt paid in one month and voided in the next rendered "−-300,00 €"); none of the three queries paginated, and the largest staging company already holds 836 receipts against PostgREST's silent 1000-row cap, so the balance would have under-reported cash with no failure signal; `calcCashSummary` had no test; an unknown `source_type` made real cash vanish from the balance rather than merely be miscategorised; and the two new cards rendered a decimal point instead of the German comma.
  - **What the merge gate proved and what it did not.** Staging holds zero cash movements, zero receipts and zero Gehaltsquittung payments across 19 companies, so every comparison in the parity script had a third term of exactly zero: it proved the two formulas equivalent and never exercised the divergence.
  - **The seeded check that does exercise it has now run on staging**, inside a transaction that ended in `ROLLBACK`, acting as the e2e test company's own admin under RLS rather than as a superuser: a driver, a salary of 300,00 € for March 2026, `confirm_salary_cash_payment` for 300,00 € dated 15.03.2026, then `void_salary_cash_receipt`. The payment produced receipt `GQ-2026-0001` and exactly one outgoing movement of 300,00 € in 2026-03; the void marked the receipt `voided` and produced one incoming movement of 300,00 € in 2026-09 — today's month, because a storno is booked on the day of the void. Net per month: 2026-03 is −300,00 €, 2026-09 is +300,00 €. The documented cash-book rule therefore holds against the live RPCs, not only in theory.
  - **Its limit:** that verified the database side — the RPCs write the movements with the right month attribution. It did not verify the screen, which rests on the four `calcCashSummary` tests PR #43 added, covering the same month boundary and the void landing in the next month. Nothing was left behind on staging, so a check against the rendered Bargeldbestand figures would still need data seeded and kept.
- **A cash salary payment is now a Gehaltsquittung (PR #69, plan 4.3d), what to know:**
  - **The defect it fixes is a ledger one, not a missing button.** `SalaryDetailsModal` inserted into `salary_payments` directly, so a payment added with `payment_type: 'cash'` wrote **no `cash_movements` row** — the money left the till and the Bargeldbestand did not move. The three Gehaltsquittung RPCs are the only writers of that ledger. The row also had no receipt, so `paymentRowActions` (which keys on `source_type = 'gehaltsquittung'`) had nothing to hang PR #49's preview button on. Adding a cash payment now hands the salary, the amount and the date to the existing `GehaltsquittungModal`, preselected and opening on its **amount** step, where the balance and the *Ort der Zahlung* are; the confirmation writes all three rows in one transaction and the lock, the badge and the preview appear on the new row by themselves.
  - **The existing dialog is opened, not copied.** `useGehaltsquittungFlow` holds the request id kept until the database answers, its resume out of `sessionStorage` after a reload, the pre-send balance re-read, and the `overlapping_salary` / `overpayment` / `request_id_conflict` refusals. A second client for `confirm_salary_cash_payment` would have to keep all of that identical, and the failure mode of drift is a payment booked twice. The one new option is `preselect`; **an unanswered confirmation still wins over it**, because that one may already be booked.
  - **The rule is keyed on the origin of the write, never on `payment_type` alone**, and that is the part not to touch. The weekly "Bar zurück" (`weekly_cash_difference`) is also stored as cash, and CLAUDE.md is explicit that it counts as paid and never moves cash — a rule of "type is cash → receipt" would book a payout from a till that was never opened. `src/utils/salaryPaymentWrite.ts` is that decision, pure and tested without a database; `handleWeeklyCashPayment` asks it too and throws if it ever answers anything but `insert`.
  - **A stored cash row is frozen in its amount and its payment type**, and the form disables both fields rather than refusing on submit. The review of this PR found the hole: `paymentRowActions` gives the pencil to every non-`gehaltsquittung` row, so a legacy cash payment of 100,00 € could be edited to 5.000,00 € — 4.900,00 € more asserted as paid in cash with no ledger row anywhere, the same defect through a different door, reachable on any legacy row by anyone with salaries-edit. Date and description carry no cash claim and stay editable. The way to correct such a row is to delete it and record it again, which now creates the receipt and moves the till, and the message says exactly that (`sal.payment.cashRowLocked`) — there is nothing to void, because the row predates receipts.
  - **Nothing is backfilled, and what that leaves standing is worth stating plainly: every cash payment recorded before 17.09.2026 still asserts money that left the till with no `cash_movements` row behind it, and no migration corrects them.** The Bargeldbestand of any company that recorded cash salary payments before this release is therefore high by the sum of those rows, permanently. They keep their row and their delete button; they get no retroactive receipt. The other door into an untracked cash payment — create it as a bank transfer, then edit its type to cash — was open before this PR and is now refused by name (`sal.payment.cashNeedsReceipt`), because `confirm_salary_cash_payment` writes its own row and cannot adopt one.
  - **A salary whose period overlaps another row of the same driver can now take no cash payment at all, and that is a deliberate capability regression.** Before this PR such a payment was a plain INSERT and succeeded; now it is a Gehaltsquittung, and `confirm_salary_cash_payment` refuses an overlapping salary (`overlapping_salary`). **The owner decided on 17.09.2026 that the refusal stays**: he merges the two rows by hand before paying, and the system keeps refusing until he has. So there is no fallback path and none should be added. What the PR does instead is make the refusal actionable — it is shown in the payment form **before the form closes**, beside the type select while a bank transfer is still one click away, and it **names the conflicting row**: its period and its due amount, because one staging company holds 16 overlapping pairs and another holds 25 salary rows in one company, where "these rows overlap" is not something anyone can act on. A bank transfer is unaffected.
  - **The overlap rule is spelled once, and both screens read it.** PR #71 merged the same day with `src/utils/salaryPeriodOverlap.ts`, the browser's mirror of the RPC's condition, and marks overlapping rows on the salaries list; its own commit message noted that `findOverlappingSalary` in `salaryCashReceiptFlow.ts` made the same comparison and that folding the two together was a follow-up. This PR is that follow-up: `findOverlappingSalary` is now the single-row form of `findOverlappingSalaryPeriods` and holds no comparison of its own, so **the row the payment form names is the first row the salaries badge lists**, decided by one function. Both agree that a **shared boundary day is an overlap** — the RPC compares with `<=` and `>=` — and that two consecutive periods (one ending the day before the next begins) are not; `salaryCashReceiptFlow.test.ts` pins both, because two spellings of one rule is how the two screens come to tell the user different things about what the database will accept.
  - **No SQL.** Nothing under `supabase/migrations/` or `tests/rls/`, so the kit needs no run for this branch. Typecheck ratchet unchanged at 228; vitest 1460 passed.
  - **Not verified:** nothing was run against staging or any database. The end-to-end behaviour is the code path PR #34 and PR #43 already exercise, but this entry point into it has not been clicked through.
- **Merging overlapping salary rows (PR #73), what to know:**
  - The other half of #71. The owner merges the rows himself, so the Gehälter screen now **deletes a salary row**; before this no screen did, and "by hand" meant a direct database edit while `confirm_salary_cash_payment` went on refusing every cash payment for the 5 drivers of the one production company that holds 16 overlapping pairs. The pair is a hand-entered calendar month beside the business month the app computes: **deleting the hand-entered one is the whole merge.**
  - **Editing a period was built and then removed, and it must not come back without reading why.** The full reasoning is in the header of `src/utils/salaryRowEdit.ts`; the first reason alone is fatal. `SalariesManagement` matches a driver's stored row to the selected period by **exact equality of both ends**, so a row widened to `01.03.–31.03.` no longer matches the computed business range `02.03.–29.03.`: `calc.salary_id` goes undefined, the table falls back to a recomputed `amount_due`, and the stored `netto_salary`, `total_paid`, `paid_at` and `status` vanish from the screen — a part-paid driver is redrawn as *unpaid, 0,00 paid*. The badge then **stays** (the widened row overlaps the computed range with no id to exclude) and the next click on *Zahlungen verwalten* runs `ensureSalaryExists` and inserts a **third** row. The widen would have undone itself and left a fresh overlap, sixteen times over. Three more: a widened start crossing a week boundary re-files issued Gehaltsquittungen under a different `business_month` while the Overview still filters by calendar month; the due figure is never recomputed, so the receipt the driver signs would state a period the amount was never computed for; and nothing stops a widen storing a *new* overlap, there being no CHECK and no exclusion constraint.
  - **A false warning was removed with it.** The delete confirmation used to say "no other period covers this one — those days will be in no salary record" whenever no single remaining row contained the deleted period. That is false for exactly the case it appeared in: a week belongs to the month containing its Monday, so `01.03.2026` belongs to business **February** and `30.–31.03.` to business **April**, and the adjacent rows already hold them. That warning is what would have pushed the owner into widening. The confirmation now names the periods that remain and claims nothing about coverage.
  - **No migration, and that was established before any UI was written.** `20260917130000` already gives `salaries` all four policies with `current_role_permits('salaries', true)` gating DELETE as well as INSERT, and the RLS kit already pins it: `matrix.sql:1210` has `salaries` `D` at `'Y.'` for the editor, supervisor and company administrator and `'..'` for anon, the viewer and a platform account. Grants are argued from those cells plus the `salaries` UPDATE `SalaryDetailsModal.tsx:273` already runs in production — **not** from a live database, which nothing in this PR touched.
  - **Where it lives and why.** A new `SalaryPeriodsModal`, on the Gehälter screen, reached from the amber badge and from the actions cell — not in `SalaryDetailsModal`. The table shows one line per driver for the *selected* period and the overlapping row is usually outside it, so a merge needs both sides at once; the dialog lists every row of the one driver out of the rows the screen already loaded (the `groupSalaryPeriodsByDriver` index #71 built is now its own `useMemo`, read by both). And opening `SalaryDetailsModal` calls `ensureSalaryExists`, which *creates* a row.
  - **Deleting refuses two ways, and the second is the one the database does not make for us.** A `salary_cash_receipts` row blocks it for good (`ON DELETE RESTRICT`, pinned as 23503 by `tests/rls/salary-cash.sql:361`) — and the check reads the **receipts**, not the payments, because a *voided* receipt keeps its row while its payment is gone, so reading payments alone would offer a delete the database answers with a bare 23503. Ordinary `salary_payments` block it too, and there the application is the only guard: that foreign key is `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so the database would take them away silently.
  - **The decision is re-taken against a fresh read of that one row's children immediately before the DELETE**, not against the map loaded when the dialog opened — otherwise a payment recorded in another tab while the dialog sat open would be cascaded away and reported as a clean success. **This narrows the window, it does not close it:** a gap remains between that read and the DELETE, and only a `SECURITY DEFINER` function checking and deleting in one transaction would remove it. That is a migration and an owner decision, deliberately not slipped into a screen change. Both child reads go through `fetchAllPaginated`, because a truncated payment list on a destructive path reads as "fewer payments hang off this row than really do".
  - **Zero rows back from the DELETE is read, not trusted**, because a refused DELETE reports no error — and the row is looked for before the caller is blamed, so "someone else already deleted it" is not reported as a permission problem. The gate is `salaryRowWriteRefusal(receiptScope(...), can('salaries','edit'))`, the two terms the policy carries; the scope term is **not** redundant, because `AuthContext.can` returns true for every platform account while `get_active_company_id()` is NULL for one.
  - **The payments refusal names the row's own period and says to select it first**, because *Zahlungen verwalten* opens the payments of the period selected on the screen behind the dialog, not of the row named in the message.
  - `src/utils/salaryRowEdit.ts` is the pure half, 19 tests. Rebased onto `2aa0795` (after #72). Ratchet unchanged at 228; vitest 58 files, 1689 passed, 7 skipped. **No SQL, so the kit needs no run for this branch.**
  - **Not verified: the screen was never rendered.** There is no component test harness (`vitest.config.ts` is `environment: 'node'` and includes `.test.ts` only), and the branch was built under an instruction not to touch the VPS or any database, so neither a staging click-through nor a local run against real data happened. **Clicking it through on staging, on the e2e test company and not a real customer, is the first thing to do after the deploy** — including the 23503 message mapping, which has never seen a real PostgreSQL response.
- **A Gehaltsquittung's number carries the salary's year (owner decision 17.09.2026, PR #75), what to know:**
  - It answers the open question above. `confirm_salary_cash_payment` keyed its counter on `EXTRACT(year FROM p_payment_date)`; migration `20260919160000` keys it on `v_byear` instead — **one assignment**, and `v_byear` is already sitting there two statements above, from `get_business_month(v_salary.period_start)`.
  - **Which year, and the evidence.** The business year of `period_start`, not its calendar year. Rule 7 of `20260914140000` already says "The receipt's month is `get_business_month(period_start)`"; the row already stores that answer as `business_month` / `business_year` and indexes the archive on `(company_id, driver_id, business_year, business_month)`. The business month is this product's month everywhere — `get_business_month()` in SQL, `utils/weekCalculations.ts` in the browser, `abrechnung_weekly`, the Stundennachweis, the Monatsplanung. Reusing it means the number's year and `business_year` are the same integer **by construction**, so they can never disagree; `period_start`'s calendar year would have been a second convention for one field, differing whenever a period starts in a week that began in the previous year.
  - **Existing receipts are not renumbered.** No UPDATE, no backfill, no counter touched. A Gehaltsquittung is a ledger document that has been printed and signed. So **both conventions live in the history**: before this release the payment's year, after it the salary's. They differ only for a salary paid in a year other than the one it belongs to. `business_year` on the row is correct either way and is what a report should group by. Production holds very few receipts and staging one test receipt, but say it rather than let it be found.
  - **What the counter's uniqueness means now.** `document_counters` is unchanged — `PRIMARY KEY (company_id, doc_type, year)`, incremented under its own row lock inside the confirming transaction, unreachable from every API role. Only the integer handed to `year` changes meaning. Gaplessness is now per (company, **salary** year): two receipts issued on one day for salaries of different years draw from different counters, that being the point. `salary_cash_receipts_number_unique UNIQUE (company_id, receipt_number)` and the `^GQ-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4,}$` CHECK need no change, the year being inside the number. **Two consequences the decision carries:** a company's numbers are no longer issued in the chronological order of its payments, and a closed year can be reopened by a late payment, still gaplessly.
  - **Nothing else reads `GQ-YYYY` expecting the payment year.** The browser never predicts a number — `salaryCashReceiptDocument.ts` prints *Nr. wird bei der Bestätigung vergeben* until the database answers — and no list, filter or export parses the year out of one. The one near miss is `signedCopyPath()` (`utils/salaryCashReceiptFlow.ts`), which files an uploaded signed copy under `{company}/{payment year}/{number}_…`; a `GQ-2025-…` copy may now sit in a `2026/` folder. **Left alone on purpose** — it is a storage folder, not a number, existing `signed_copy_path` values are absolute, and moving it would change where uploads land for nothing.
  - **The body is rewritten from the catalogue, not retyped**, the precedent `20260917130000` set for these three functions: the regexp must match exactly once or the migration fails without changing anything, and `CREATE OR REPLACE` keeps the owner, the pinned `search_path`, `SECURITY DEFINER` and the ACL. The owner is deliberately **not** moved to `CURRENT_USER`: on the live databases these belong to `postgres`, 3.3 chose a grant over an ownership change for exactly these three, and this adds no call `postgres` cannot already reach. The self-check asserts the year comes from the salary, that the assignment is read before the number is built, and that thirteen load-bearing fragments of the function (the 3.3 state gate, the role gate, both advisory locks, `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, idempotency, the overlap refusal, …) are still there — restating a function here has already lost a rule twice.
  - Backward compatible, **no `SCHEMA_EPOCH` bump**: a rollback leaves the new function in place and the previous release reads `receipt_number` as an opaque string.
  - Kit files: `supabase/migrations/20260919160000_gehaltsquittung_number_salary_year.sql` and `tests/rls/salary-cash.sql`. **The kit was not run from this branch** (no Docker here, and the branch was built under an instruction not to touch the VPS or any database) — run `npm run test:rls` before merging.
- **The Gehaltsquittung prints its Abrechnungsmonat (owner decision 18.09.2026, PR #78), what to know:**
  - **Why it exists.** With #75 the number's `GQ-YYYY` is the salary's business year. The sheet printed only `periodStart`, `periodEnd` and `paymentDate`, all three of which read 2026 for a salary whose period starts Thursday 01.01.2026 — so `GQ-2025-…` was the only "2025" on a paper going to the Steuerberater, and read as a mistake rather than as a rule. The receipt now carries **Abrechnungsmonat: Dezember 2025** beside its Zeitraum, and the number explains itself. No SQL, no migration, no change to how the number is built.
  - **The rule it preserves: a confirmed receipt prints the row the database stored.** `salary_cash_receipts.business_month` / `.business_year` were written by `confirm_salary_cash_payment` since `20260914140000` and were simply never selected; `RECEIPT_COLUMNS` (`src/lib/salaryCashReceipts.ts`) now reads them and `storedReceiptDocumentInput` is the only thing that fills `ReceiptDocumentInput.businessMonth` for a confirmed or voided receipt. Nothing recomputes it — a value derived in the browser would let a later change to the calendar rule reprint an issued document under a month other than the one it was numbered by. `salaryPaymentReceiptRow.test.ts` pins that with a row whose stored pair (12/2025) is one the period alone (01.01.2026–25.01.2026) would not obviously produce.
  - **The preview is the one place it is computed**, because no row exists yet, and it computes it from the same rule the RPC uses: `businessMonthOfPeriod()` → `getBusinessMonth()` (`utils/weekCalculations.ts`), the browser twin of `get_business_month()`. **`weekCalculations` counts months from 0 and the stored column from 1**; the `+ 1` happens once, in that one function, and a test asserts the two agree for five dates including 01.01.2026. The date is read as local calendar parts, never `new Date("YYYY-MM-DD")`, which is UTC midnight and falls back a day west of Greenwich — that would move the week, and with it the month, for every period starting on a Monday.
  - **Wording and placement, and what they cost.** The label is `Abrechnungsmonat`, the product's own German for this (nothing in `src/` named the concept before), the value a German month name and year — hard-coded German like the rest of the sheet, since the Gehaltsquittung is on the closed statutory list in `src/i18n/index.ts`. It sits in the fact row **between Zeitraum and Zahlungsdatum**, the two dates it is derived from and paid against. That row is four equal flex boxes now instead of three, so **`Zeitraum` wraps onto two lines** at its en-dash (682 px of content cannot hold a date range and three more boxes on one line, at any split). Rendered and looked at; it reads cleanly and the sheet has room to spare.
  - **The list has an `Abrechnungsmonat` column too** (`GehaltsquittungList`), `hideBelow: 'lg'`, after the period and before *Gezahlt am*, sorted by `business_year * 12 + business_month`. It reads the stored columns like the sheet does. It is a screen, not the document, so its header follows the UI language — German `Abrechnungsmonat`, English `Business month` — and the month name comes from the existing `doc.month.*` keys. Only the sheet is German in both.
  - **Not verified: the list was never rendered.** Same reason as #73 above — no component harness, and no VPS or database. The *document* was rendered: `GehaltsquittungSheet` through `react-dom/server` and headless Chrome, for a January 2026 period numbered `GQ-2025-0004` and an August one numbered `GQ-2026-0012`. Click the list through on staging after the deploy.
  - Ratchet unchanged at 228; `npx vitest run` 58 files, 1749 passed, 7 skipped; `npm run build` clean. **No SQL, so the kit needs no run for this branch.**

A follow-up replaced the indefinite spinner a failed profile load produced with a recovery screen offering retry and sign-out, behind a bounded retry policy (3 attempts, 400 then 800 ms) that is unit-tested. 126 new vitest cases. e2e 13 passed, 1 skipped — the skip is the Google spec skipping itself while the provider is off, which is the intended assertion.
